notes: Warehouses. Commodity storage was free and unbounded: player_cargo just incremented and ship capacity gated only /api/cargo/ship, never buying or holding. Holding was therefore never a decision and cornering a colony's supply cost nothing to sustain. Storage is now metered per colony against a continuous capacity slider denominated in F, not crates, because the storage problem is the value under roof: per unit pricing charged the same to shelve frayed wiring (basePrice 210) as nano filament (4100). Goods are valued WHEN THEY ENTER the shed and never marked to market, so a crash cannot silently free shelf and a spike cannot blow a lease set in good faith. Rent is 0.8% of leased capacity per day, modified by colony control (Syndicate 0.70 cheapest and unbonded, Coalition 1.30 dearest and safe) and by tension, which gives faction control a second job beyond price. Charged DAILY, not on the commodity tick: tickCommodityPrices reverts 0.25 toward target every 5 minutes so a dislocation half lives in about 12 minutes, and the only durable reason to hold is a change in the target itself, which moves over days. Arrears follow the margin call model, including running for disconnected players and re-reading live state at the deadline. Containment is the point: a shed in arrears settles from its own stock at its own colony's price and never reaches cash held for anything else, another colony's shed, equities or fund stake. Default costs that colony for 30 days, not forever, and settling in full lifts it immediately. Seven day grandfather window so nobody is called for inventory bought under free storage. SERVER RESTART REQUIRED, schema migration on boot.
